"PROJECT: G1itḥeď a Pªrt (Glitch Fighters)

Act as an experienced 3D fighting-game developer, game designer, and technical artist. Build my dream game while preserving the following vision. Do not replace, simplify, or reinterpret its core gameplay.

1. Core concept

- Platform: Mobile, landscape orientation, locked to landscape.
- Gameplay: Offline initially; online functionality is not required yet.
- Visuals: 3D fighting characters inside a 2D fighting arena (2.5D).
- Genre: Real-time fighting game.
- Matches and rounds vary depending on the game mode or event.
- Character design inspired by the atmosphere and visual style of Inside.
- The game must feel like an actual fighting game, not a turn-based game, menu-based combat, or rock-paper-scissors.

2. Essential combat gameplay

Characters must be directly controllable and fight in real time.

Required mechanics:

- Move left and right.
- Jump and crouch.
- Dodge.
- Light and heavy attacks.
- Blocking.
- Combos.
- Special attacks.
- Responsive opponents that actively approach, move, attack, and defend.
- A functional arena where both fighters physically interact.

Combat must have responsive animations, health, damage, knockback, and actual victory/defeat conditions.

The first playable milestone must contain:

- One playable fighter.
- One opponent.
- One arena.
- Fully functional real-time combat.

Do not move on to expanding the roster before this foundation works.

3. Characters and factions

The main character is G1ith:

- A teenager.
- Wears predominantly black clothing.
- Has green glitch patterns that constantly shift across his clothes.
- When using his fireball attack, the patterns temporarily turn red before returning to green.

Three enemy factions:

Pirates

- Ordinary pirates.
- Large pirate tank enemies.

Skeletons

- Inspired by the skeleton aesthetic of Prince of Persia.
- Ordinary skeletons.
- Armored skeleton tank enemies.

Gangsters

- Inspired by gangsters in Spider-Man games.
- Ordinary gangsters.
- Large gangster tank enemies.

Enemy classes:

1. Default: Uses hands to fight.
2. Melee specialist: Uses faction-specific weapons and may have a weaker ranged weapon.
3. Ranged specialist: Has weaker melee attacks but a powerful ranged weapon.
4. Tank (previously called trucks): Heavily built enemies with greater durability.

4. Arenas

Initial arenas:

- Alleyway.
- Jungle.
- Pirate ship.

All arenas must have the same dimensions and fighting space, but their environmental boundaries and walls should match their surroundings.

Environmental interactive objects are a possible future addition, not a required initial feature.

5. Game modes

PLAY

- Story Mode: Locked and marked as under development.
- Survival Mode.
- Tournaments.

Difficulty settings:

- Easy: Lower enemy damage.
- Hard: Higher enemy HP.
- Expert: Higher enemy HP and damage.

Survival

- Survive successive encounters.
- Optional roguelike card system.
- Cards have three quality levels: Good, Great, and Bad.
- Card difficulty and quality should depend on the selected difficulty.

Tournaments

- Special rules and restrictions that change how fights work.
- Example: Handcuffs prevent punching, forcing players to rely on kicks.

6. Main menu and additional sections

The title screen must contain:

- Play.
- Practice.
- Gallery.
- Settings.
- Shop.

The menu layout should have a dark, mysterious atmosphere. On the right side, display a randomly selected arena with two Gallery characters fighting as a visual showcase.

Gallery

- A two-sided character collection.
- Displays collected heroes and enemies.
- Selecting a character reveals their moves and lore.

Practice

- A free-play training environment.
- Allows the player to control an enemy.
- The practice enemy must remain stationary and cannot attack, move, use special abilities, use ranged weapons, or change fighting distance.
- Include a tutorial.

Settings and Shop

- Include these as functional menu sections without inventing unspecified systems.

7. Opening sequence and title

The game begins with a red Arabic warning:

\"لا تجعلها تشغلك عن العبادات\"

Follow it with a glitch animation:

1. A mysterious green, catlike eye appears.
2. The eye transforms into a candle.
3. The candle transforms into a diamond.
4. The diamond transforms into a magician's hat.
5. Each transformation uses distinctive glitch transitions:
   - Green and red.
   - Red and blue.
   - Blue and purple.
6. Transition to a completely black screen.
7. Reveal the title:

G1itḥeď a Pªrt

Avoid unnecessary loading screens.

8. Character switching and special identity

Character/leader switching is an important desired feature, inspired by:

- Naruto Storm.
- Demon Slayer fighting games.

Preserve this concept for development without inventing its detailed rules.

9. Art direction

- Dark, mysterious atmosphere.
- Distinctive glitch effects.
- Crimson glitch accents alongside green, blue, and purple effects.
- 3D characters with recognizable silhouettes and expressive fighting animations.
- Character designs inspired by Inside.
- Arenas must feel like actual environments rather than flat backgrounds.

10. Development requirements

- Prioritize playable gameplay over attractive but nonfunctional menus.
- Every button and mechanic must actually work.
- Do not create turn-based combat, automated battles, or choose-an-attack-and-watch gameplay.
- Mobile touch controls must be supported.
- Preserve the landscape mobile format.
- Clearly distinguish between implemented features, generated visual concepts, and planned features.
- Never claim a feature is implemented unless it has actually been tested.
- Build progressively, testing every milestone before expanding.

MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT:

I want to physically control my fighter, move around an arena, attack, defend, dodge, jump, perform combos, and fight an opponent that actively fights back.

I want a real fighting game, not a simulation of choosing fighting actions.

Preserve the original vision of G1itḥeď a Pªrt. Do not sacrifice gameplay for presentation.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
